source.edition: Henry Barclay Swete, The Old Testament in Greek According to the Septuagint, Volume I, first edition, Cambridge University Press (1887)
source.comment: Historical edition public domain in US by publication year; original page-level transcription, witness sigla and morphology require a final independent visual audit. Source metadata is identified, not an imported/reviewed full chapter.

reader_notes.text: The surviving ancient Codex Vaticanus does not preserve the opening chapters of Genesis. For those chapters Swete's printed Greek Septuagint uses other early manuscript evidence, especially Codex Alexandrinus. This is a gap in a surviving manuscript, not an omission of Genesis 1 from Swete's edition.
reader_notes.audio_policy: Deliver in an accessible source-note segment or companion transcript; do not interrupt the continuous chapter reading without a deliberate edition choice.

verses.text: In the beginning God made heaven and earth.
The earth was unseen and unformed, and darkness lay over the deep. And the Spirit of God was moving over the water.
And God said, “Let there be light.” And there was light.
God saw that the light was good, and God separated the light from the darkness.
God called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night. And evening came, and morning came: one day.

notes: Original provisional English sample from Greek Septuagint; multiple style variants and word-choice questions are documented in notes/ot/GEN/001.md.
